question.leadin: This king first swore allegiance to Edward Longshanks of England in 1296.
question.text: Name this king who eventually won his country's independence from England in 1327.
question.clue: This man was excommunicated by Clement V after his involvement in in the murder of John Comyn, who was nephew to this monarchs predecessor, John Balliol.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about famous plots in history.
swap.text: King James I was targeted during this plot, in which a group of Catholics led by Robert Catesby attempted to blow up a section of Parliament. Guy Fawkes Night, often celebrated in the UK with bonfires, marks the anniversary of this plot's failure.
swap.answerHtml: the Gunpowder Plot [or the Gunpowder Treason Plot or the Jesuit Treason]
swap.clue: Among those principals was Thomas Percy, who rented the room at the center of the plan.

question.text: This first ruler from the House of Normandy ruled from 1066-1087 following his victory at the Battle of Hastings.
question.answerHtml: William I [accept William the Conqueror or William the Bastard; prompt on “William”]
question.clue: An Archbishop of Canterbury named Stigand stands next to this ruler in one depiction commissioned by his half-brother Odo.

swap.text: This British prime minister and proponent of appeasement was given a hero's welcome after negotiating the Munich Agreement in 1938, but would resign the next year in favor of Winston Churchill.
swap.clue: The polemic Guilty Men was written during his premiership and listed him first among the offenders.

question.leadin: This conflict saw the sinking of the General Belgrano by the submarine Conqueror.
question.text: Name this war that saw the Battles of Goose Green and San Carlos, as well as the sinking of the HMS Sheffield. This war was fought over a territory one of the belligerents refers to as Las Islas Malvinas.
question.clue: This conflict began when one side's troops landed on April 2, and ended when they were forced to give up the territorial capital of Port Stanley in mid-June of the same year.

swap.text: Clashes between the York's and Lancaster's went as far back as the 1300's following the death of the Black Prince, the heir apparent to this king who was in power during English victories at Poitiers and Crecy during the Hundred Years War.
swap.clue: This king imposed price controls to address a manpower shortage caused by the Black Death in the Statute of Laborers.

question.leadin: She isn't Elizabeth I, but this woman made a rousing speech about English courage in anticipation of the Earl of Surrey's victory at Flodden Field.
question.text: The book The Education of A Christian Woman by Juan Luis Vives was commissioned by this wife of Arthur, the son of Henry VII.
question.clue: She served as regent for one year while her husband joined Maximilian I in defeating French forces at Guinegate.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about Britain's struggle against France during the Napoleonic Wars.
swap.text: Horatio Nelson died leading British ships to victory over the French and Spanish navies at this October 1805 sea battle off the coast of Spain.
swap.clue: The British commander at this battle, who lost no ships, declared that "England expects that every man will do his duty," before being shot by a sniper.

question.leadin: This site is located two miles south of a similarly named site made of wood in Wiltshire, England.
question.text: Name this large, circular stone monument, which is theorized to have served some burial or astronomical-related function.
question.clue: This monument is made of a circular series of holes, some of which contain large rocks.

swap.text: The New Model Army won this decisive June 1645 battle against the forces of Prince Rupert at a site about 50 miles north of Oxford.
swap.clue: The victorious side at this battle, which was fought in Northamptonshire, took damage on its left wing under the command of Henry Ireton, who faced an assault by Prince Rupert.

question.text: During the revolt, the peasants destroyed Marshalsea prison and this debtors' prison located by its namesake London river and street. John Donne and William Penn were imprisoned in this location.
question.clue: This notorious prison, which was destroyed during both Wat Tyler's rebellion and the Gordon Riots. Prisoners in this prison could bribe wardens to live outside the walls in a practice termed the "Liberty of the Rules."

swap.leadin: Identify the following about the Industrial Revolution in England.
swap.text: During the Industrial Revolution, the New Poor Law of 1834 made it so that anyone who was unemployed and did not enter into these institutions would not get relief. These places exchanged shelter to the poor for menial labor.
swap.clue: Residents of these so-called "bastilles," such as a young Charlie Chaplin, were often given menial tasks like grinding bones.

question.leadin: You are a wealthy member of the European bourgeoisie in 19th century Europe. Answer some questions about expanding and profiting off of land ownership.
question.text: You can grab some land in the Scottish Highlands through this process of appropriation of common land. After a General Act regarding this process, commissioners could approve areas for it without consulting parliament.
question.clue: The terms "Levellers" and "Diggers" originally referred to people who took action against this practice.

swap.leadin: This man's Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum is a massive treatise of alchemy compiled from various famous authors.
swap.text: Name this English collector, numismatist, and Freemason. He donated his cabinet of curiosities, much of which was obtained from the Tradescants of Lambeth, to his namesake museum.

question.leadin: This person's life is attested to in part by four separate wills made from 1394 to 1416, and The Book of Margery Kempe describes a visit regarding their revelations.
question.text: Name this fourteenth-century anchoress and author of the Showings.
question.answerHtml: Julian of Norwich [or Juliana of Norwich; accept Lady Juliana, Dame Juliana or Mother Juliana; prompt on Julian or Juliana alone]

swap.leadin: He got one of his noble titles by marrying Anne Beauchamp, and he died at the Battle of Barnet.
swap.text: Name this man, who left his captaincy of Calais to lead a coup and capture the king at Northampton. Later the same year, he became the second earl of Salisbury when his father, the first earl, was killed at Wakefield.
swap.answerHtml: Richard Neville, 16th earl of Warwick [accept either; prompt on Kingmaker]
swap.clue: This man, who was killed at the Battle of Barnet several years after tensions erupted between him and his king over the king's marriage to Elizabeth Woodville. He was known as "the Kingmaker."

question.leadin: Among its provisions were the abolition of the practice of compounding.
question.text: Name this piece of legislation spearheaded by Benjamin Disraeli that extended the franchise to nearly one million men.
question.answerHtml: Reform Bill of 1867 [or Second Reform Bill or Representation of the People Act of 1867; accept "Act" for "Bill"]

swap.text: This "Queen of the Music Hall" sang "Now You've Got Your Khaki On" for the war effort. This scandalous singer rose to fame with songs like "Oh Mr Porter" and "The Boy I Love Is Up in the Gallery."
swap.clue: This singer, who supported the 1907 strike, was known as the "Queen of the Music Hall." She sang songs dripping with innuendo, such as "She'd Never Had Her Ticket Punched Before," as well as hits like "The Boy I Love is Up in the Gallery" and "My Old Man."

question.leadin: Name these dissenting groups during the era of the English Civil War, FTPE.
question.text: This nonconformist group founded by Gerrard Winstanley in 1649 championed the formation of self-sufficient agricultural communities of the common people and announced that Britain had been under foreign subjugation since the "Norman yoke."
question.answerHtml: the Diggers or True Levellers (DO NOT accept or prompt on “Levellers”)
question.clue: This group of Protestant Agrarian communists that practiced communal farming and advocated egalitarian living, which was founded by Gerrard Winstanley.

swap.leadin: This grandfather of Alfred the Great and descendant of Cerdic lived in exile at the court of Charlemagne before conquering Sussex and Northumbria.
swap.text: Name this Anglo-Saxon ruler who took title Bretwalda as king of Wessex. He defeated the Welsh at Hingston Down and the Mercians at Ellendun.
